Broncos vs. Rams picks, prediction, player props: Expert's best bets for Sunday Night Football in NFL Week 3 Mile High altitude and a stout Denver defense give the underdog hosts a distinct edge against Los Angeles in a tight prime-time battle By Will Brinson Sep 27, 2026 at 8:07 pm ET • 3 min read Add CBS Sports on Google Imagn Images The NFL never disappoints, and Week 3 of the 2026 season appears to be no different. Just when we think we know everything, we know very little. Sunday Night Football will be a good test of how little we know, with the Broncos playing Jekyll and Hyde the first two weeks of the season and in the two different halves against the Jaguars last week. The total is down to 44.5. Bet on Sunday Night Football at DraftKings, where new users get $150 in bonus bets after they spend $5+: The Rams pulled a similar move in Week 1 versus Week 2, and now they're favored on the road in prime time in a really tough place to play early in the year. They opened with a loss to the 49ers but bounced back by cruising past the Giants 28-6 on Monday night in Week 2. Los Angeles is a 1.5-point favorite, and the Over/Under for total points is 44.5. Get a $55 bonus after $25 in trades by claiming the latest Kalshi promo code CBSSPORTS55 here : Best bets for Sunday Night Football Broncos +2.5 I'm *the* Rams guy -- we joked about what the number would need to be in order for me to NOT take the Rams on our SportsLine picks show Wednesday. And I was on the Rams earlier in the week, but I'm pivoting now, with me thinking the altitude plus the Broncos defense and the high level of this Denver team meaning that the Broncos probably shouldn't be underdogs at home this early in the year. Aaron Donald returned to the NFL last week and played a decent number of snaps, but it's going to be tough for him to ramp up at Mile High. Sean Payton can coach around the weaknesses of his team, and while I expect the Rams to very much keep this competitive and for it to a be a low-scoring close game, my spidey sense says the Broncos find a way to win late, and if not, it's a field goal walk-off situation for either team, making these points extremely valuable. Sunday Night Football player props Jaylen Waddle 6+ receptions (+127, DraftKings) You'll see the Over for Waddle's receptions above heavily juiced, but just know that we're playing his SIX reception number at +127 on DraftKings here. I like both, obviously, and think this is a good ladder spot for Waddle. In Week 1 he was non-existent, which is shocking given that the Broncos traded a first-round pick for him this offseason. Week 2 was very different and the Broncos reaped the benefits. I fully expect Davis Webb and Sean Payton to get Waddle heavily involved, especially since the Broncos running back depth chart is extremely depleted. Kyren Williams over 12.5 receiving yards (-116, DraftKings) Williams and Blake Corum are very much in a timeshare at running back at this point and I don't think that will change. It makes backing their rush props difficult. But it also means Williams receiving prop is way down. He's always good for several targets in the short-yardage area and 12.5 isn't that much to ask from the standout running back, especially when Denver's ability to bring pressure plus the likely absence of Puka Nacua meaning safety valves for Matthew Stafford will likely be a play-calling focus for McVay. Bet on NFL player props and more at BetMGM: Sunday Night Football anytime touchdowns Davante Adams (+115, DraftKings) Davante went off in Week 2 after a slow Week 1, and while this matchup is much more difficult for the superstar wide receiver, he's getting a fantastic price here on an anytime touchdown. The Broncos and Patrick Surtain will make life difficult, and I definitely don't see him chasing 200 receiving yards. But at plus money with his usage and red-zone scoring ability? This is a no-brainer. Bo Nix (+475, DraftKings) This number has me giddy! Bo Nix is almost 5-1 to score a touchdown??? Yeah the Rams defense is great and yeah Nix hasn't been running like we'd prefer with eight rushes for eight total yards. But he's always a threat to run and against this defense I think he'll take off a few more times. And I actually foresee some red-zone dial ups to activate his legs in tough spots, making this number extremely tantalizing. His first-touchdown-scorer number of 18-1 is real nice as well. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Opening-week workloads point us toward a few early NFL player props for Week 2 Derrick Henry leads a pair of rushing props coming off heavy Week 1 usage Keep reading for our three early NFL props to target in Week 2, starting with Thursday night One week of football doesn’t settle much, but it does show how teams plan to use their best players. For early Week 2 props, I want players with a defined role and a number they can beat without repeating their best game. That starts with a Bills quarterback hosting a Detroit defense that just allowed 410 passing yards, then moves to a pair of rushing props driven by workload. Here are the NFL props I’m targeting for Week 2. NFL Week 2 Player Props to Target Player Prop Projected Line Josh Allen (BUF) Over Passing Yards 220.5 Derrick Henry (BAL) Over Rushing Yards 78.5 Caleb Williams (CHI) Over Rushing Yards 20.5 These projected targets are not posted sportsbook lines. Check the current lines at BetMGM and use our BetMGM promo code to sign up. You can also compare NFL betting apps before placing a bet. NFL Player Prop Pick: Josh Allen Passing Yards Josh Allen didn’t need big volume to carve up the Texans in Week 1. He completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions in a 36-31 win at Houston. He spread the ball around, too. DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid combined for 230 receiving yards, so Allen isn’t leaning on one target to move the offense. That makes Buffalo a tough team to slow down through the air. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to Tyler Shough in their opener. He went 35-of-56 with three touchdowns and two interceptions, and Detroit still escaped with a 31-30 overtime win. That yardage came on a heavy workload, and Allen doesn’t need anything close to it. He threw for 334 yards on 29 attempts, which is 27 fewer than Shough. A 220.5 target leaves plenty of room. Allen can fall well short of his Week 1 performance and still cash the over, and he gets the Lions at home on Thursday night. Early Bet: Josh Allen over 220.5 passing yards NFL Player Prop Pick: Derrick Henry Rushing Yards Baltimore gave Derrick Henry plenty of work in the opener. He carried 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns in a 41-23 win at Indianapolis. For a yardage prop, the carries matter more than the scores. The Ravens kept feeding Henry in a game they won comfortably, and that kind of volume can get him over this number even if the big runs don’t show up. New Orleans just spent an overtime game trying to slow down Jahmyr Gibbs, without much luck. Gibbs ran 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 5.4 yards per carry. Now the Saints have to deal with Henry. Henry averaged 6.0 yards per carry against the Colts, but this bet doesn’t need that kind of efficiency. Even at 4.0 per carry, 20 attempts would put him over the target. If Baltimore gives him anything close to his Week 1 volume at home on Sunday, 78.5 is a number I’m happy to bet the over on. Early Bet: Derrick Henry over 78.5 rushing yards NFL Player Prop Pick: Caleb Williams Rushing Yards Caleb Williams ran a lot more than usual in Week 1. He carried 10 times for 65 yards and two touchdowns, well above the 4.5 carries per game he averaged last season. That’s the kind of usage you want to see for a quarterback rushing prop. His 2025 numbers already support this bet. Williams finished with 77 carries for 388 yards and three touchdowns over 17 games, which works out to 22.8 rushing yards per game. The 20.5 target sits below that average before Week 1 even enters the picture. The carries could settle back down, and that’s fine. Williams averaged 5.0 yards per carry last season, so he doesn’t need double-digit attempts to reach the low 20s. With the Vikings visiting Chicago on Sunday, I’m taking the over at 20.5. His average last season was already above this target, and he ran more often in the opener. Sean Payton, who is entering his third season in charge of the Broncos, has made the postseason in 11 of his 18 seasons as a head coach. He has never finished with fewer than seven wins, effectively putting his teams in playoff contention every single year dating back to 2006. Eight of his 11 playoff berths have coincided with division titles, too, including last year’s. Denver is sitting at +225 to repeat as AFC West champions, which is good for third behind both the Chiefs and Chargers. However, the Broncos actually account for 34% of the bets to win the AFC West, narrowly outpacing the Chiefs and Chargers’ respective 32%. And in terms of the total handle, Denver leads the pack at 40%, signifying a sharp lean in their favor. Analysis We are entering Year 3 of Sean Payton and Bo Nix, not to mention all the other returning skill position players. Denver also went out and added Jaylen Waddle to supplement Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin, Pat Bryant, Marvin Mims Jr., Lil’Jordan Humphrey, Evan Engram, J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. They also bring back most key contributors from their defense, even using their top draft pick on Tyler Onyedim to make up for lineman John Franklin-Myers leaving in free agency. Considering that unit held opponents to the third-fewest points per game last season, it’s easy to see them being elite again in 2026. Going against a Chargers squad that hasn’t won a division crown since 2009 and a Chiefs team that showed signs of age and injury in 2025, the Broncos should be in the driver’s seat once again in 2026. Best AFC West Playoff Future Chargers to Make the Playoffs (-168) Betting Splits Ranking Bets 11th Handle 18th Why bettors are backing the Chargers The Chargers rank around the middle of the pack in terms of both bets and handle when it comes to making the playoffs. They are slightly above average with the 11th-most Make the Playoff bets and rank slightly below average with the 18th-most handle in that market. What is worth noting, however, is that they account for the third-fewest bets to miss the playoffs, as well as the smallest handle in that market. Basically, very few people and even fewer sharp bettors are banking on Los Angeles to miss the playoffs. Analysis Los Angeles went 11-6 in each of Jim Harbaugh’s first two seasons at the helm, earning a Wild Card berth both times. Dating back to Harbaugh’s time in charge of the 49ers, he has led his team to the playoffs in five of six opportunities. The Chargers also enter this campaign in a much healthier position than they were in last year, in which they thrived despite their offensive line issues. Pro Football Focus ranked their O-line 30th out of 32 units in the NFL, with Joe Alt missing 11 games and Rashawn Slater missing all 17. Their respective returns – plus the arrival of offensive guru Mike McDaniel at coordinator – could vault Justin Herbert into the league’s top tier of quarterbacks. Omarion Hampton might break out as well, if first round pick Jake Slaughter can replace the retired Bradley Bozeman and injured Tyler Biadasz at center. The Chargers have boasted a top-10 scoring defense in both of Harbaugh’s seasons, too, so there’s reason to believe they can weather the losses of Da’Shawn Hand and Otito Ogbonnia up front. Best AFC West Win Total Bet Raiders Over 5.5 Wins (-146) Betting Splits Percentage Bets 73% Handle 91% Why bettors are taking the over The majority of bettors are putting their money on the Raiders to win at least six games, despite the fact that they won just four games in 2024 and three in 2025. But with Antonio Pierce and Pete Carroll gone and reigning Super Bowl champion offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak now in charge, things could be different in Vegas. On top of the general public support, there is a pretty substantial sharp lean in the Raiders’ favor. 91% of the handle is on the Raiders to clear 5.5 wins, which is about as close to universal support as you can get from a total money perspective. Analysis Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza may be at polar opposite ends of their careers, but their arrivals are reason for confidence in Las Vegas. The top rookie and seasoned veteran should fit nice into Kubiak’s system, which brought Sam Darnold back from the dead in Seattle. Although they may not have the weapons to cobble together an elite offense, the Raiders have Kolton Miller returning at left tackle and Tyler Linderbaum entering the fray at center. That should give them an O-line that PFF ranks higher than No. 32, like they did last season, beyond Kubiak’s offense traditionally minimizing talent deficiencies up front. The Raiders have the Browns, Cardinals and Titans on the schedule after Thanksgiving, at which point the team will probably have come into its own. Games against the Jets, Saints and Dolphins look winnable as well, to say nothing of any potential upsets. Keep an eye on Week 18 against the Chiefs, when Kansas City may have already locked up their playoff seeding. Best AFC West Player Prop Bet Fernando Mendoza Under 12.5 Passing TDs (-110) Betting Splits Percentage Bets 4% Handle 43% Why bettors are backing the under There isn’t widespread support in Fernando Mendoza coming in under 12.5 passing touchdowns, with only 4% of the bets in that market coming in on that side of the line. There is a massive sharp lean, however, with 43% of the handle on the under. So while the public as a whole is getting swept up in the hype for the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, the people putting more money behind their bets aren’t quite as convinced. Analysis While there is reason to believe the Raiders will take a leap forward in 2026, their new franchise quarterback might not have a lot to do with it. Cousins, who is freshly 38 years old, started 14 games in 2024 and appeared in 10 in 2025. He led Atlanta to a 12-10 record when he started, despite all of that coming after his 2023 Achilles surgery. Cousins posted an unimpressive 87.2 passer rating during his time with the Falcons, a noticeable decline from his 99.9 mark between 2015 and 2023, but he was still a steady enough veteran presence to start over Michael Penix Jr. when healthy. Based on the start of training camp and the preseason, the starting job in Las Vegas belongs to Cousins. The Raiders also have a pretty tough schedule through their Week 13 bye, which would make installing Mendoza particularly difficult. I think the rookie sees the field in 2026, but not in any serious capacity until the final five games. So unless Cousins gets hurt, Mendoza probably won’t have much of a chance to stuff the stat sheet this season. Best AFC West Award Bet Patrick Mahomes to Win Comeback Player of the Year (+185) Betting Splits Percentage Bets 22% Handle 38% Why bettors are backing Mahomes Mahomes has the shortest odds to win Comeback Player of the Year by a pretty wide margin, with his +185 odds sitting pretty high above Jayden Daniels’ +450 and Kyler Murray’s +600. So it isn’t much of a surprise that Mahomes accounts for a market-high 22% of the bets – twice as many bets as Murray in second. There is a sharp lean towards Mahomes, too, since he is drawing 38% of the handle. Analysis This is Patrick Mahomes we’re talking about. Prior to 2025, he had placed top-seven in MVP voting in five the previous seven seasons. He is coming off the worst campaign of his career – he recorded just six wins, 22 touchdowns, 3,587 yards and an 89.6 passing rating – as well as a torn ACL in December. If Mahomes can guide Kansas City back to the playoffs and just come close to the 13 wins, 4,581 yards and 35 touchdowns he was averaging between 2018 and 2024, that should be enough for him to take home some hardware. When it comes to direct competition, I like Mahomes to reemerge rather than more slight, injury-prone hopefuls like Daniels and Murray. Aaron Donald unretiring is still a question mark, too, as is his potential impact should he rejoin the Rams after all. The narrative is also on Mahomes’ side, plus the fact that quarterbacks won the award seven straight years from 2018 to 2024. Drew Brees, Tom Brady, Peyton Manning, Andrew Luck and Joe Burrow have all won CPOTY in the past 20 years, and it only feels fitting for Mahomes to join that club. Green Bay Packers to make the playoffs (-112) Injuries cost the Green Bay Packers dearly toward the end of the 2025 season, the most impactful of which saw Micah Parsons suffer a season-ending ACL injury in Week 15. The Packers also had to cope without tight end Tucker Kraft after he sustained the same injury beforehand in Week 9, the other most notable absence in the lineup. While Parsons will be out for the first five or six weeks, the Packers face teams they should be able to cope with in his absence , including the New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Matthew Stafford Over 3925.5 passing yards (-114) Stafford threw for a career-best 4,707 passing yards last season, which was enough to win MVP. While he is among the MVP odds contenders, Stafford is closer to 10th than first. He has eclipsed the required total in four of the previous six seasons , with one of the exclusions due to an injury-riddled 2022 season. The Rams might not put up the gaudy numbers they managed last year, but I expect them to be among the league's top offenses again. Unless Stafford gets injured, a distinct possibility, I expect him to have another proficient passing season under center. 💡 More NFL playoff picks Our Andrew Reid also weighs in with some of his best picks to reach the postseason . While they might not finish with the AFC's best record, the Broncos have the coach and personnel in place to comfortably make the playoffs for a third straight season. Bo Nix, who has a clean bill of health entering preseason, has shown he's more than capable of running Sean Payton's system.
